solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flexible accessory releasing workers on time

indicators.note: releasing means letting go, so these letters are dropped from the longer word

parts.note: an accessory or add-on is a supplement

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: men are workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: A handy gadget that frees staff to finish punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN followed by T gives MENT, which 'releasing' takes off the end of SUPPLEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something flexible bends easily, as a lithe body does.

clue.text: Lowest fare always for poet in coach

indicators.note: in places the poetic word inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a stagecoach, or stage, is a horse-drawn coach
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A poet always travels in the cheapest seats on the coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowest fare' is a ticket class, not food; poets shorten ever to two syllables-worth of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest class of passage on a ship, so it is the lowest fare.

clue.text: Groom roped in mate to be best man?

indicators.note: to groom is to tidy and rearrange, so these letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A bridegroom gets his friend involved as best man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' looks like the wedding's main man but is the anagram signal on ROPEDINMATE; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To predominate is to prevail or come out on top, a whimsical reading of being the best man.

clue.text: Large rotund regulars ignored forte

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: dropping the regularly spaced letters of rotund leaves its other alternate letters

explanation.surface: A big, round musician skipped the strong passage.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignoring R, T and N from 'rotund' leaves OUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Forte is the musical direction meaning play loudly, so it is an instruction for loud.

clue.text: A distress call brings in top firefighter

indicators.note: brings in means the distress signal takes the other word inside it

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
to top is to beat, which is to best

explanation.surface: A mayday summons the finest fire officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firefighter' suggests a person; it is a fire-resisting material.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos was used in fireproof suits and blankets, so it fought fire in a playful sense.

clue.text: Smallholder traps superior bear

indicators.note: traps means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: read as small (S) plus holder
U is the abbreviation for upper class, so superior

explanation.surface: A farmer with a few acres catches a top-quality bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smallholder' splits as S (small) and HOLDER; U goes in after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a burden is to bear it, as in shouldering responsibility.

clue.text: Catholic English copper with minion casing clubs

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: casing means the servant word wraps round the card suit

parts.note: a minion is a servant, a menial
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: An English Catholic police officer with a lackey containing a golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised 'Catholic' suggests the church, but the definition is the lower-case sense, universal.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic in its lower-case sense means universal or wide-ranging, as ecumenical does for all churches.

clue.text: Dry Irish politician hosts European

indicators.note: hosts means the politician holds the next letter inside

parts.note: TD (Teachta Dala) is a member of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: A teetotal Irish politician entertains a visitor from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: To ted is to spread newly cut hay out so that it can dry.

clue.text: Hot work here with German in cast

indicators.note: in places the German word inside the throwing word

parts.note: to cast is to throw, to shy
mit is German for with

explanation.surface: A sweltering job with a German among the actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith's forge is a workplace of heat and red-hot metal.

clue.text: Primate breaks rule governing Mass

indicators.note: breaks means the letters are broken up and reformed

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: An archbishop flouts the regulation governing the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop beside 'Mass', but it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemur is an example of a primate, the order including monkeys and apes.

clue.text: Top director sacking four

indicators.note: sacking means firing, so these letters are thrown out

parts.note: a company director is an executive
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A senior boss lays off four staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top director' reads as one phrase, but 'Top' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Top is slang for kill, and to execute is to put to death.

clue.text: Religious group's Oedipus complex

indicators.note: a complex is an intricate arrangement, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A Catholic movement's Freudian hang-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus Dei is a Roman Catholic organisation, an institution of the church.

clue.text: Bouncer beginning to make space

parts.note: a kangaroo, or roo, bounds along

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman starting to clear a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' suggests a doorman; it is the kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Room means space, as in room to move.

clue.text: Like ball gowns and some balls

definitions.meaning: in cricket a delivery pitched well up to the batsman is called this

explanation.definitionFit: Ball gowns reach the ankles, and in cricket a pitched-up delivery is described by the same phrase.

clue.text: Golf partner played round with relative

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: round means the shuffled letters go around the joining word
played means the letters are performed in a new order

parts.note: with means and, joining things together

explanation.surface: A golfing partner has played a round alongside a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges partner and 'round' places that around the word for 'with'; 'round' looks like a round of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandparent is a relative, an example of a family member two generations up.

clue.text: Bobby's fly

definitions.meaning: a dated slang word for a policeman, from his blue uniform

explanation.definitionFit: A policeman in old slang, and a big metallic blowfly; Bobby is British slang for a police officer.

clue.text: Horrible bear caught

indicators.note: caught as in heard, signalling a word that sounds like another

parts.note: the grizzly is a North American brown bear

explanation.surface: A dreadful bear has been trapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Grisly means gruesome and causing horror, a near synonym.

clue.text: Big bird left one clutching nut? On the contrary

indicators.note: clutching means one piece holds the other
on the contrary means the holding goes the other way round, the nut doing the clutching

parts.note: a pecan is a nut
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A large bird abandoned someone gripping a nut, or rather the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutching' suggests LI holds the nut; 'On the contrary' reverses that, so PECAN holds LI.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelican is an example of a large water bird with a pouched bill.

clue.text: Christian who makes flights

definitions.meaning: ... Christian led the mutiny on the Bounty
an arrow-maker, who fits feathers or flights to arrows

explanation.definitionFit: The Bounty mutineer's first name, and a maker of arrows; 'Christian' disguises a surname-first reading.

clue.text: I go over to visit Los Angeles for hero-worshipping

indicators.note: over to says the go word is passed along to the end, after the others

parts.note: to do a place is to visit it as a tourist
a go is a try, an attempt

explanation.surface: A traveller crosses to see Los Angeles out of devotion to a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visit' here is DO, as tourists 'do' a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is the worship of idols, extended to excessive admiration of a person.

clue.text: Faint, swallowing green drink

indicators.note: swallowing means the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: faint means pale, lacking colour
a green is a grassy area, a lea

explanation.surface: Someone feeling weak downs a green beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' is a grassy field here, not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale ale is a type of beer, so an example of a drink.

clue.text: Frank's auxiliaries also in police

indicators.note: in places the joining word inside the detective branch

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
also means and, in addition

explanation.surface: Frank's assistants are also in the police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auxiliaries' gives the answer a second way: CAN and DID are both auxiliary verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means open and honest, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Leaves container label covering each barrel

indicators.note: covering means the label wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a label is a tag

explanation.surface: A label is wrapped round each barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb but is tea leaves; EAB goes inside TAG after T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea bag holds tea leaves for brewing, so it contains leaves.

clue.text: Main canoe wrecked

indicators.note: wrecked means broken apart, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A boat smashed on the high seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a literary term for the high seas, the ocean.

clue.text: Method when grilling star on air with discretion

indicators.note: on air means as broadcast, so heard spoken

parts.note: a star or celebrity is an icon
discretion is tact

explanation.surface: A broadcasting technique for interrogating a celebrity tactfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grilling' means questioning, not cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Interrogators hold a suspect's gaze as a technique when questioning hard.

clue.text: Herb avoids middle one of four bars at Lord's

definitions.text: one of four bars at Lord's

indicators.note: avoids middle means the centre letter of the herb is left out

parts.note: basil is a herb

explanation.surface: A herb skips the middle drink of four at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is a London cricket ground; each pair of stumps carries two small crosspieces, four per pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bail is a small wooden crosspiece resting on the stumps, two at each end.

clue.text: Gouda cheese suppresses thirst

indicators.note: suppresses means the phrase holds the word down inside it

explanation.surface: Dutch cheese quells a craving.
explanation.definitionFit: To thirst for something is to yearn or long for it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Black and white bust commands college entrance

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: bust means broken, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A monochrome sculpture of a head orders entry to the college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commands' links the colour and college pieces; 'entrance' is the verb meaning enchant, not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance is to cast a spell over, to enchant or charm.

clue.text: Attempt to win with rings

parts.note: rings are round, so each gives O

explanation.surface: A suitor tries to win her hand with rings.
explanation.definitionFit: To woo is to court, trying to win someone's affection or support.

clue.text: Very old soldier owns new company in Paris

indicators.note: owns means the soldier holds the other letters

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant
Cie is the French abbreviation for compagnie, company

explanation.surface: An elderly soldier owns a new business in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means belonging to the distant past, so extremely old.

clue.text: Travel round Spain with this writer to test some maths

indicators.note: round means travel's letters go around the country code

parts.note: to travel is to go
E is the international vehicle code for Spain
the setter refers to themselves, so me
to test is to try

explanation.surface: Journeying around Spain with the setter to examine arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometry is a branch of mathematics, an example of maths.

clue.text: Guard who's maybe boxed first of several competitors

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the word

parts.note: the competitors in an event are its entry

explanation.surface: A guard, perhaps a boxer, beats several rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxed' points to a sentry box, not a boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier on guard duty, who may stand in a sentry box.
